name: Jehiah
overview: Jehiah was a male Levite who served as one of the gatekeepers for the ark, a significant role in the worship and religious life of Israel. His position as a gatekeeper highlights his responsibility in guarding the sacred space associated with the presence of God. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Jehiah means 'y-h-v-h lives,' reflecting a theophoric element that honors the living God. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:24, underscores a connection to the divine name YHWH, though it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Jehiah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Levi, the priestly tribe, according to 1 Chronicles 15:24. Beyond this tribal affiliation, Scripture does not record any further family relationships for him.
scriptureSignificance: Jehiah's role as a gatekeeper for the ark places him within the sacred duties entrusted to the Levites during the transportation and safeguarding of the ark of the covenant. This responsibility underscores the reverence and order God commanded in worship practices. His inclusion in the biblical record affirms the importance of faithful service in maintaining the holiness of God's presence among His people.
